stages.closes: Answer the DESIGN interview from declared defaults (`[design.interview]`) or a declared automation, and record it on the ledger, so no DESIGN gate waits for a person.

criteria.reason: DESIGN is designed to talk to a person (CLAUDE.md, the six-phase model); it is autonomous only where every gate it raises is answered by a declared, ledgered rule.

stages.question: Of the DESIGN-phase gates answered in the window, how many were answered by the gate-timeout sweep or a declared automation rather than a person?
stages.title: DESIGN resolves without a person

stages.closes: Fewer BUILD escalations (budget, repair or attempts exhausted) per finished job: the escalations are the gates a person answers.

criteria.reason: BUILD is designed to run unattended; an exhaustion gate is the point where it stops and asks a person.

stages.question: Of the BUILD jobs that finished and the BUILD escalations raised in the window, how many were finished jobs rather than gates waiting for a person?
stages.title: BUILD runs unattended

stages.closes: A running worker that keeps every paid engine's login fresh (#1295 rechecks at half its life); an engine whose login lapses drops out of rotation until someone logs in.

criteria.reason: The 2026-09-30 scan found every paid job deferred once a login was a day old; a lapsed login is the dropout.

stages.question: Of the declared paid engines, how many passed a login check within its time-to-live at the cutoff?
stages.title: Paid engines stay available

stages.closes: A declared, ledgered rule for REVIEW's `approval` gate, which today carries no default and can never time out; until then REVIEW keeps its person by design.

criteria.reason: A gate kind without a timeout default waits for a person however long (the operator's ruling of 2026-09-30, #1299).
What the declarations allow is not evidence they are used: the answered gates are.

stages.question: Can each gate REVIEW raises resolve without a person, and did the ones answered in the window?
stages.title: REVIEW resolves without a person

stages.closes: A review that answers every head in time (#1316 bounds the call; #1303 gives it the files), and a merge that waits for the verdict.

criteria.reason: A merge without a verdict is a merge a person vouched for, or nobody did.

stages.question: Of the pull requests merged into the integration branch in the window, how many carry a review verdict (passed or blocked) at their merged head?
stages.title: The pull-request review reaches a verdict

stages.closes: A weekly review-canary measurement that meets `[pr_automation.review_canary]`'s floor for the settings the review runs with.

criteria.reason: An unattended approver leans on the review; a review whose recall is unmeasured or under the floor is not something to lean on (`vibey-gh review-canary status`).

stages.question: Does the latest review-canary measurement meet the declared recall and false-positive floor, for the review's current settings and corpus, within its age limit?
stages.title: The review's verdict is trustworthy

stages.closes: A workflow that calls the delegated approver once every gate is green, and `PR review / gate` declared as a required status check on the integration branch.

criteria.reason: Sub-doctrine 12.f: approval while nobody watches comes from the operator's declared approver, applying a standard it did not choose.
A gate that is not required can be merged past; the approver's standard rests on the gate being green.

stages.question: Of the pull requests merged in the window, how many carry an approving review by the delegated approver, and is the review gate a required check?
stages.title: Approval comes from the delegated approver

stages.closes: Merges made by the merge train after an approval, so the ruleset is satisfied rather than bypassed.

criteria.reason: A merge by the operator's account is a merge by the operator.
The integration branch requires one approving review; a merge without one went in through the ruleset bypass (12.d: no gate routed around).

stages.question: Of the pull requests merged in the window, how many were merged by an account other than the operator's, and how many carried the approving review the ruleset requires (no bypass)?
stages.title: Merges land without the operator

stages.closes: Promotion started by the merge train or its schedule and merged without the operator's account; a release workflow that publishes on every push to the release branch.

criteria.reason: A promotion dispatched by hand is a hand step. A share of runs would hide it: the merge train starts hundreds of runs that find nothing to promote, so the count of hand dispatches is the honest figure (at most one a week is partial).
A promotion merged by the operator's account is the operator's act.
A failed publish needs a person to repair and re-run it.

stages.question: In the window, how many promotions did a person dispatch by hand, how many promotions merged into the release branch without the operator, and how many release publishes succeeded?
stages.title: Promotion and release run without hand steps

stages.closes: A green integration branch whose failures are real and repaired by a change, not by pressing re-run on a flake.

criteria.reason: A red integration branch stops the merge train until someone repairs it.
A re-run is a person deciding a failure was a flake.

stages.question: Of the CI runs on the integration branch in the window, how many succeeded, and how many needed a re-run?
stages.title: CI stays green without human re-runs

stages.closes: A worker and the bridge installed as services (`vibey supervisor install`) and draining the queue, with projects reaching DONE.

criteria.reason: DONE is the only completion the six-phase model records; nothing else is delivery.
A queue with no event in a day has no worker draining it.

stages.question: Did any project reach DONE in the window, and has the queue recorded any event within a day of the cutoff?
stages.title: The queue delivers projects to DONE

criteria.reason: a sample of 3, under the declared minimum of 10
the window holds no sample (0 of 0)
